cosy-lesson.title: "AI is the opposite of taking risks...": Madonna

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Opposite – completely different from something else.

p.em: Example: Happy is the natural opposite of sad.

cosy-blockquote.p: Risk – the possibility of something bad happening.

p.em: Example: Starting a new business involves a high financial risk.

cosy-blockquote.p: Art – paintings, music, and books made by human creativity.

p.em: Example: I love visiting museums to see historical art.

cosy-blockquote.p: Computer – an electronic device for storing and processing data.

p.em: Example: I use my office computer to write emails and documents.

cosy-blockquote.p: Rule – an official statement that tells you what you must or must not do.

p.em: Example: You must follow the safety rules in the laboratory.

cosy-blockquote.p: Song – a short piece of music with words that you sing.

p.em: Example: She sings a cheerful song when she cooks dinner.

cosy-blockquote.p: Creative – good at producing new and original ideas.

p.em: Example: My sister is very creative and makes beautiful handmade cards.

cosy-blockquote.p: Different – not the same as another thing; distinct.

p.em: Example: My daily routine is different on Saturdays and Sundays.

cosy-blockquote.p: Feeling – an emotion or physical sensation.

p.em: Example: I have a wonderful feeling about my English class today.

cosy-blockquote.p: Simple ≠ Complex – easily understood or done; presenting no difficulty ≠ consisting of many different and connected parts.

p.em: Example: The basic idea was wonderfully simple, but the actual execution turned out to be incredibly complex.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What is the opposite of a boring day at the office?
★ What is the opposite of your favorite subject at school?

Why is starting a new career a big risk?
★ Do you like taking risks, or do you prefer to feel safe?

Where can we see beautiful art in your city?
★ Do you have any paintings or art on your bedroom wall?

How often do you use your home computer?
★ Do you prefer to study on your phone or on a computer?

What is the most important rule in a library?
★ Do you follow strict rules easily, or do you like freedom?

What is your favorite English song?
★ Do you enjoy singing songs when you are in the shower?

Why are children so creative when they play?
★ What is your most creative hobby?

Why do different people like different styles of music?
★ Do you and your best friend have different favorite songs?

How do you express a feeling of happiness to others?
★ Do you share your true feelings easily with your family?

Is it easy to write a simple poem?
★ What is the simplest recipe you know how to cook?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Visual comparison: Singing vs Computer programming. - 🎤Singing (Voice) - 💻Coding AI (Machine)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will enable us to digitize and share our experience of opposite directly. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you personally adapt if opposite became entirely obsolete in tomorrow's world?

The rapid speed of modern society will eventually make risk an obsolete concept. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be willing to use technology to artificially boost your capacity for risk?

Future educational systems will prioritize the cultivation of art over traditional academic skills. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with art?

As artificial intelligence advances, machines will exhibit a superior capacity for computer compared to humans. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach the value of computer to children?

In the coming decades, rule will become a highly commercialized luxury commodity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where rule is fully managed or monitored by digital algorithms?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our collective ability to practice song. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where song is increasingly rare?

Future generations will look back at our current understanding of creative with deep skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about creative to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true different incredibly difficult to maintain in the future. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees different at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's capacity for feeling rather than wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope feeling will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the mystery of simple. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your experience of simple, would you still value it?

ul.li: Incorrect: The AI can to write song → Correct: AI can write songs ((Can + infinitive without 'to', plural noun 'songs'))
Incorrect: I am listen to Madonna → Correct: I listen to Madonna ((Simple present structure))
Incorrect: It depend of your taste → Correct: It depends on your taste ((Depends + on, singular verb s))
